forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No new major announcements. Metaculus combined forecast still centres AGI arrival around mid-2030 (80% CI: 2027-2043). Kalshi traders price ~42% for OpenAI AGI by 2030. Anthropic Claude Mythos 5 (10T params) and Gemini 3.1 released in April 2026 but no credible AGI claim. Hold at 25%.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Metaculus median AGI arrival now mid-2030 (+3pp)
Claude Mythos 5 (10T params) and Gemini 3.1 in April (+2pp)
Continued capital deployment by leading labs (+2pp)
Hassabis and others flagging 2026 as breakthrough year (+2pp)
factors_down: No credible lab has declared AGI (-4pp)
key_uncertainties: What threshold counts as 'AGI' for this question's resolution
Whether scaling returns hold at 10T+ parameter models
Timing of autonomous R&D demonstrations

update_triggers.up: A major lab publicly declares AGI, or 3+ leading researchers endorse a specific milestone
update_triggers.down: Pause or stall in frontier capability gains, or major labs walk back timelines

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: McKinsey now down to ~40,000 headcount with ~10% non-client-facing cuts underway; Accenture Q2 FY2026 revenue $18B and raised full-year local-currency growth guidance to 3-5%. AI disrupting juniors but revenue base still growing. No directional shift. Hold at 18%.
forecasts.base_rate: Sector-level 33%+ declines in 5 years are rare (<15% of professional-services episodes)
factors_up: Grad hiring down sharply across Big 4/MBB (+2pp)
factors_down: Global consulting revenue still >$375B and growing (-3pp)
High-value strategy work still commanding premiums (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether value and jobs track together or diverge
Pace at which AI substitutes senior advisory work
Whether economic consultancy narrowly-defined fares differently from management consulting

update_triggers.up: A major firm reports double-digit revenue decline explicitly blamed on AI
update_triggers.down: Sustained >10% revenue growth among the top 5 firms through 2027

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: YouGov 12-13 April: Reform 24%, Con 19%, Grn 18%, Lab 17%, LD 13%. More in Common April MRP projects Reform 324 seats (1 short of majority), Labour down to 101 seats. Labour now in a four-way fight for second place. Nudge down from 5% to 4%.
forecasts.base_rate: Incumbent parties polling <20% ~3 years out almost never recover to be largest party
factors_up: Reform support could prove shallow under scrutiny (+2pp)
FPTP can produce surprises on narrow vote shares (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour in 4th place on vote intention (-4pp)
Only 101 seats in the April MRP (-3pp)
Green Party eating Labour urban strongholds (-2pp)
Reform 5pp clear on headline voting intention (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform can hold coalition through governance scrutiny
Timing of the next election (still likely 2029)
Whether Labour replaces leadership before election

update_triggers.up: Reform scandal or internal split; Labour closes gap to <5pp
update_triggers.down: Reform consolidates lead above 30%; Labour drops to single digits

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Metaculus combined forecast continues to point to mid-2030 median for AGI arrival with 80% CI spanning 2027-2043 — the central mass is comfortably inside the 2035 deadline. April launches (Claude Mythos 5, Gemini 3.1) reinforce breakthrough narrative. Hold at 73%.
forecasts.base_rate: Metaculus-weighted probability of AGI before 2035 implied at ~70-80%
factors_down: Upper tail of CI extends past 2035 (-4pp)
Regulatory or compute constraints could slow pace (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether continual learning / world models progress as expected
Energy and chip constraints in late-2020s
Definitional threshold for 'AGI'

update_triggers.up: Autonomous multi-month R&D demonstrations by frontier labs

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Taiwan's Penghu live-fire drills (10 April) and PLA's April three-phase exercise continue the familiar tempo. DNI assessment still reads PRC as not planning near-term invasion. CNN noted unexplained two-week pause in PLA flights earlier in March. No escalation. Hold at 10%.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical base rate for major-power attacks on specified adversaries over ~4 years ~5-10%
factors_up: APS upgrades on PLA armor suggest amphibious prep (+1pp)
Xi's 2027 PLA readiness target still in sight (+1pp)
factors_down: DNI: China 'does not currently plan invasion' (-4pp)
Economic costs of blockade enormous for PRC (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Internal PRC political dynamics
US election cycle and signalling in 2028
Whether a grey-zone action could cross the 72-hour blockade threshold

update_triggers.up: Sustained naval cordon around Taiwan ports
update_triggers.down: Credible cross-strait détente or official PRC timeline push-out

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Bank of England now expects CPI 3.0-3.5% through Q2-Q3 2026 on Middle East energy shock (up from 2.1% Q2 in Feb Report). Oxford Economics sees 4% possible in H2 2026. Only ~8 months of CPI prints remaining for a sub-2% reading. Probability pushed down from 2% to 1%.
forecasts.base_rate: P(sub-2% CPI print in any single month given BoE projecting 3%+) ~2-3%
factors_up: Sharp energy reversal possible if Middle East tensions ease (+1pp)
Base-effect months in late 2026 could drop year-on-year (+1pp)
key_uncertainties: Energy-price path in H2 2026
Whether Middle East conflict de-escalates
GBP/USD volatility feeding into import prices

update_triggers.up: Oil price below $60 sustained for >1 month; core services inflation <2%
update_triggers.down: Another energy spike; services inflation above 4%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Trailer reached 1 billion views (industry first). Polymarket 45.5% for highest-grossing 2026 film. Variety and koimoi tracking imply opening weekend alone could push franchise into $4B club. Presales showing steady upward momentum. Small uptick to 96%.
forecasts.base_rate: MCU Spider-Man films post-Homecoming: 2 of 3 have grossed >$1.1B globally; No Way Home hit $1.9B
factors_up: 5 months of tailwinds before 31 July release (+2pp)
factors_down: Without multiverse hook, matching No Way Home hype is hard (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Chinese release status and revenue
Whether Avengers: Doomsday cannibalises audience
Critical reception at launch

update_triggers.down: Marketing stall; surprise negative reviews at premiere

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Anthropic at $30B ARR (passed OpenAI), OpenAI at $25B: combined ~$55B April 2026. Altimeter suggests Anthropic ARR could triple by year-end. Even with conservative growth, $70B combined is highly plausible by Q4 2026. Nudge up from 95% to 96%.
forecasts.base_rate: Given current ~$55B combined and sector growth rates, P(>$70B by Dec 2026) high
factors_up: Combined ARR already ~$55B with 8 months runway (+5pp)
factors_down: Revenue recognition definitions vary by reporter (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 'ARR' per Bloomberg/FT/The Information aligns with company internal metrics
Timing of any Q4 price cuts or enterprise contract resets
Macro shock risk through remainder of 2026

update_triggers.up: Either company reports >$40B ARR before Q4
update_triggers.down: A credible report of revenue stall or contract cancellations

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: OBR March 2026 forecast avg 1.5% across its forecast window; Nov 2025 revision took TFP from 1.1% to 0.8% medium-term. IMF still at 1.2-1.4% near-term. Question is right at the threshold; AI productivity gains remain the key swing factor. Hold at 44%.
forecasts.base_rate: UK annual real GDP avg 2010-2019 was ~1.9%; 2020s trending lower — base rate near 40-50%
factors_up: Population ageing could reverse via automation (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour supply growth falling to 0.5% by 2030 (-3pp)
IFS skeptical of OBR productivity assumptions (-2pp)
Persistent UK productivity gap vs US (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Magnitude and timing of AI productivity gains
Migration policy trajectory
Energy-cost competitiveness for UK industry

update_triggers.up: ONS productivity growth >1.5% sustained for 2+ years
